turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste either of our time. Who decided to put a zero in Owen's gradebook, and why did my son find out on his phone in the middle of a class?
"Out of time." I've been in this chair for one minute, and I'm not leaving until you answer my question: who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard before it went in?
Just say okay and I'll write it up as resolved. Okay?
No. Nothing is resolved until that zero comes off, and if you write this up as anything else, I'll be in the principal's office before you've saved the file.
I've answered that. The zero, Hale: who decided, and when?
Ms. Kalinowski. I need you to say okay.
No. I'm writing down that you asked me three times to say "okay" instead of answering a single question about my son.
